name: char
title: Format a character vector in a tibble

origin.description: Keep a character vector and record how a tibble should shorten it.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A character vector. A number fails is.character(x).

arguments.name: min_chars
arguments.text: Minimum width stored on the pillar attribute. NULL omits it.

arguments.name: shorten
arguments.text: Omitted or NULL stores nothing. Otherwise one of "back", "front", "mid", or "abbreviate". The match is exact.

origin.details: The strings are not shortened here. format of the pillar attribute is the type label, which is vec_ptype_full. It starts with pillar_char, appends (min_chars) when that argument is set, and appends a mark for shorten: back is >, front is <, and mid is |. The stored choice abbreviate is not one of those marks, so the label gains nothing. A missing string stays missing. The abbreviation is char, or abbr only when the stored shorten is exactly abbr.
origin.value: The same character data, with class pillar_char and a pillar attribute.
origin.example:
x <- char(c("a", "bb"), min_chars = 5, shorten = "mid")
x
format(attr(x, "pillar"))
vctrs::vec_ptype_abbr(x)
y <- char(c("a", NA))
y
format(attr(y, "pillar"))
vctrs::vec_ptype_abbr(y)
z <- char("hello", min_chars = 3, shorten = "abbreviate")
format(attr(z, "pillar"))
vctrs::vec_ptype_abbr(z)

translation.description: The same stored options. None is a missing string, and a string or a list of strings is the data.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A string, None, or a list of strings. None is a missing string. A number is rejected.

arguments.name: min_chars
arguments.text: Stored and printed inside the type label. None omits it. A number is pasted the way R pastes a double.

arguments.name: shorten
arguments.text: None, or one of "back", "front", "mid", or "abbreviate". A prefix such as "b" is rejected.

translation.details: The result keeps the data and is marked pillar_char. format_pillar_char_attr of the pillar attribute is vec_ptype_full. abbreviate adds no mark. vec_ptype_abbr is char, or abbr only when the stored shorten is exactly abbr. Column formatting is not done here.
translation.value: A PillarChar. data is the string or the list. pillar holds min_chars and shorten.
translation.example:
from pillar.char import char, format_pillar_char_attr, vec_ptype_abbr

x = char(["a", "bb"], min_chars=5, shorten="mid")
print(x.data)
print(format_pillar_char_attr(x.pillar))
print(vec_ptype_abbr(x))
y = char(["a", None])
print(y.data)
print(format_pillar_char_attr(y.pillar))
print(vec_ptype_abbr(y))
z = char("hello", min_chars=3, shorten="abbreviate")
print(format_pillar_char_attr(z.pillar))
print(vec_ptype_abbr(z))
